Ever wonder what happened to the front porch?

Industry observers note that the front porch used to play an important role in everyday life. Neighbors who weren’t necessarily close friends saw each other, stopped to talk, and maintained a sense of community. Then daily life moved indoors. Air-conditioning made staying inside more comfortable, television pulled families into the living room, and backyard patios offered more privacy so you didn’t have to say “hi” to the overly talkative neighbor.

Recent findings suggest that there was no single moment when the front porch disappeared. It just gradually became less central to the way people connected, and faded away.

The lunch break is headed in the same direction.

Recent findings suggest that technology has made it possible to collaborate across locations and time zones, while AI is helping work move faster than ever. But constant connectivity has also weakened the boundaries around the workday. An open hour at noon can swiftly become another meeting or a chance to catch up on work.

Peer pressure plays a role too. Employees see colleagues and leaders eating at their desks or scheduling meetings over lunch with a polite, “Sorry, it was the only free time I could find.” Eventually, skipping lunch becomes an unwritten expectation rather than an individual choice. And when that behavior is rewarded with recognition and career growth, the expectation becomes even harder to challenge.

Yet lunch is one of the few natural opportunities during the workday to step away and connect with colleagues without an agenda. It also gives employees a chance to decompress, take a walk, and mentally reset before tackling the rest of the day. Leaders who want sustainable performance should make sure that opportunity doesn’t disappear.

Industry observers note that you don’t have to mandate how employees spend lunch. Some people want to eat with colleagues. Others prefer to take a walk, run an errand, or simply be alone.

The point is to create a culture where stepping away feels like a normal choice. And it requires looking at the signals your workplace sends about availability, performance, and connection.

In a recent development, 1. Create space that can’t automatically become another meeting.

It has been revealed that if every open block on a calendar is considered schedulable, lunch will always be at risk. Consider establishing meeting-free windows during the day so employees have protected time to recharge.

According to recent reports, adapt that approach for global and frontline teams instead of assuming the same time works for everyone. Employees across time zones and operating environments may need different windows, but the principle is the same: Build recovery into the work day.

According to recent reports, 2. Model the behavior you want.

Culture is a collection of the norms, values, and behaviors that employees see around them every day. And nothing is more vital for building culture than what employees see from their leaders. If leaders are regularly scheduling meetings during lunch, it’s a signal that the break isn’t protected. New employees in particular pick up such signals, and swiftly learn which behaviors are associated with success (and failure) in their new team or organization.

Your own calendar also sends a powerful message. Protecting and taking your lunch break is critical, as is extending the same respect to your team during their breaks. These small, visible behaviors speak louder than words.

3. Treat skipped lunches as an key signal.

Recent findings suggest that understanding and measuring workplace culture requires listening in different ways. Surveys alone don’t cut it. Paying attention to skipped lunches can be part of that strategy. And while working through lunch might ultimately be a personal preference, when it becomes the norm, it tells you something about your organization.

Sources indicate that if employees feel they can’t step away for even 30 minutes without falling behind, that’s a strong signal that the always-on mentality is rampant in your organization. Burnout in these cultures can be prolific, and workloads, staffing levels, and meeting demands should be questioned.

Industry observers note that but consider the unwritten expectations, too. What happens when employees say no? Is their commitment to the team or organization questioned? Are they no longer seen as top performers?

The Simple AI Framework I Use to Cut Administrative Waste

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
  • When I opened my first physical therapy practice, I believed growth depended on seeing more patients.
  • Sources indicate that years later, after building therapy, staffing and hospice companies, I see artificial intelligence the same way I see any business tool: Its value comes from solving a real operational problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

When I opened my first physical therapy practice, I believed growth depended on seeing more patients. That mindset worked for a while, until I realized my team and I were spending hours every day on paperwork, scheduling and insurance tasks instead of patient care. Administrative work had quietly become the biggest obstacle to growth.

Sources indicate that years later, after building therapy, staffing and hospice companies, I see artificial intelligence the same way I see any business tool: Its value comes from solving a real operational problem. AI should give your people more time to serve customers and build relationships. Everything else is secondary. That philosophy has shaped how we use technology across our businesses.

Recent findings suggest that spend a week identifying every repetitive task that eats up valuable time. Look for work that follows the same steps every day and requires little judgment. Those processes usually deliver the fastest return when automated.

According to recent reports, in health care, charting, appointment scheduling and insurance verification quickly rose to the top of our list. Every industry has its own version of these tasks. Find them before you buy any technology.

Industry observers note that resist the urge to automate everything at once. Doing so can overwhelm you and your team, and it makes it hard to tell which changes worked and which flopped.

Start with the one to three administrative processes that consume the most hours each week. For us, documentation was the obvious first choice. AI-assisted transcription dramatically reduced the time clinicians spent writing notes, so they could focus on patients instead of keyboards.

We also introduced AI tools for scheduling and insurance verification. Those systems reduced delays and freed employees to handle conversations that required empathy and critical thinking.

Many leaders evaluate AI by asking whether the software costs less than another employee. I prefer a different question: How many productive hours did the technology return to the business?

According to recent reports, if documentation falls from 30 minutes to five minutes per appointment, those recovered hours create measurable capacity. Teams can serve more customers, improve quality or simply leave work on time. Revenue often follows, but the first win is reclaimed time.

According to recent reports, tracking time savings also keeps expectations realistic. Every automation project should produce measurable improvements before you expand it to another department.

Every AI project deserves a simple scorecard. Track how many hours employees save each week, how promptly customers get a response, how many errors disappear from the process and how your team feels after the change. Those measurements show whether the technology is delivering real value or just adding another subscription to the budget.

Review these metrics every month. Small improvements often compound into significant operational gains over time. Consistent measurement also helps employees see the purpose behind each new tool, which builds confidence and speeds adoption across the organization.

Burnout rarely begins with meaningful work. It usually begins with repetitive work.

It has been revealed that few health care professionals entered the field because they loved paperwork, and entrepreneurs in every industry can relate. Endless administrative duties drain energy that could go to customers, employees or strategic planning.

When AI removes repetitive work, people get back to the work that inspired them in the first place, and burnout drops as a result. In our businesses, clinicians give more attention to patient conversations because documentation happens in the background. That shift improves both the employee experience and the customer experience.

It has been revealed that successful adoption comes from discipline, not speed. Begin with one department. Select one workflow. Define one success metric. Once that process delivers consistent results, move on to the next opportunity.

This phased approach builds confidence throughout the organization. Employees see practical improvements instead of another technology initiative that creates extra work. Leaders also gain reliable data before making larger investments.

Small wins create momentum that large transformations rarely achieve on day one.

One common misconception is that AI is meant to replace people. It isn’t.

Recent findings suggest that technology should strengthen human capability, not replace human judgment. Every automation decision we make comes back to the same question: Will this give our people more time for work that requires experience, compassion and creative thinking?

That principle has guided our investments, from AI documentation to administrative automation. Technology handles repetition. People handle relationships. Together, they build stronger businesses than either could alone.

In a recent development, once we put these changes in place, the difference was almost immediate. Clinicians spent less time on documentation after appointments and more time engaging with patients during them. Front office teams fielded fewer routine calls because scheduling and administrative questions moved through AI-powered workflows, which reduced delays and made the experience smoother for everyone.

Industry observers note that what surprised me most was the ripple effect. Employees felt less overwhelmed because they could focus on work that required their expertise. Leaders had better visibility into operations because we were measuring performance instead of reacting to problems. Those improvements gave us the confidence to expand AI into other areas of the business, one process at a time.

It has been revealed that the experience reinforced something I’ve believed throughout my career: Sustainable growth comes from building systems that free talented people to do what they do best. AI became one more tool that helped us deliver better care, strengthen our operations and prepare our businesses for the next stage of growth.

In a recent development, the Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the latest one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any time soon. The firm has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games and next week's offerings.

If you're looking for more freebies, you can check out our list of the 25 best free PC games to play right now, or for more options, the 25 best free games to play on multiple platforms.

It has been revealed that this week, you can get a welcome gift pack for Firestone: Idle Clicker Online RPG, and you can help a pair of penguins out in the co-op platformer Bread & Fred. The welcome pack for Firestone is valued at $100, and it includes an exclusive Talia skin, chests, avatars and gems. Newly introduced players must reach stage 15 to claim it.

Next week, you can get Strange Antiquities for free. Run a shop full of occult antiques in the eerie town of Undermere, uncover sinister secrets, help the locals out, and do pet your adorable shop cat.

Industry observers note that we're keeping a running list of every free game that Epic users have been able to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really made its mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a powerful PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Look at the list below to see the frankly ridiculous list of free games that have been available.

#8. In the AI era, dependability is the key to customer loyalty

In the AI era, dependability is the key to customer loyalty

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1777 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that before I released my own organization, I worked as a web developer for a New York media company.
  • In a recent development, before I released my own company, I worked as a web developer for a New York media company.
  • In today’s fast-changing tech landscape, customer expectations are evolving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that before I released my own organization, I worked as a web developer for a New York media company. One of my colleagues was a coding savant. They could build a webpage in mere hours, an incredible feat in the early aughts. They could identify bugs and rapidly come up with smart solutions. But they also frequently disappeared in the middle of the workday and took personal days with little to no notice. My colleague was reliable in their work, but not dependable day-to-day. Employees—and organizations—need both to provide real value. In today’s fast-changing tech landscape, customer expectations are evolving. Customers expect businesses to be reliable and digital experiences to work as promised. At the same time, they’re becoming wary of the tech race. In a recent survey of about 3,500 U.S. consumers about their digital lives, 77% said tech companies focus more on outpacing the competition than on solving real user problems. What separates leading organizations in the AI era is not reliability alone, but dependability at every step. Here’s how leaders and organizations can deliver on that promise. Make every customer experience consistent Having a product or service work the way you need it to is key. No doubt, customers take note. In the above-mentioned survey, three-quarters of consumers reported that new tech features improved their lives and that digital experiences were becoming more personalized. At the same time, fewer than 30% said they strongly agree with that sentiment. The takeaway for businesses: There’s room for improvement. Where can businesses identify those areas for improvement? One strategy is ensuring that the entire user experience is 24/7 consistent. Every interaction along the customer journey, from initial inquiries to troubleshooting, should provide the same level of care and attention. Artificial intelligence can help make that possible. Customized AI agents, for example, can respond to common inquiries around the clock. When faced with more complex or nuanced issues, they can escalate the matter to human representatives. This ensures customers can connect with your company whenever they need to, and without requiring employees to be always on. Consistency also means ensuring customers receive the same information across channels, whether they’re perusing the website, DMing with a chatbot via an app, or speaking with an employee on the phone. For customers, the result isn’t just a reliable product or service—it’s feeling heard and seen. That’s where dependability makes a difference. Customers build trust when every interaction feels responsive and aligns with what the organization has promised. Ensure every interaction feels like your brand Every interaction between customers and your company is an opportunity to build a relationship—or weaken an existing one. Especially in the age of AI, your company’s voice has to be cohesive, whether customers are chatting with an employee or a chatbot. As noted in Harvard Business Review, chatbots are becoming the frontline of customer interactions—and they can shape how customers perceive your brand, from its personality and values to its approach to customer service. What’s more, the HBR article highlights research showing that people who interacted with a warm, supportive AI companion felt closer to the chatbot than to colleagues, acquaintances, and even friends. Owners of a more task-oriented assistant, on the other hand, felt less connected to it than to their human relationships. The implication for brands: How AI communicates impacts the customer experience, as well as the kind of relationship customers believe they have with a company. For starters, customer-facing AI tools should reflect your brand identity. With a chatbot, for example, you can begin by defining its personality; whether it’s a supportive coach, an empathetic companion, or a sophisticated advisor. Decide the kind of information it handles and when conversations should be handed off to a human. AI-powered chatbots should do more than just sound like your brand. They should deliver the kind of relationship that reflects your company’s mission and values. Anticipate customer needs and act on them In the AI era, one of the biggest competitive advantages is anticipating customers’ needs, sometimes even before they’re aware of them. Consider a large language model like ChatGPT, which predicts what you might need next, encouraging users to continue engaging with it. For instance, you prompt ChatGPT to generate an outline; it does, then asks whether you’d like a draft introduction as well. Whether or not you say yes is your choice, but the option is there. Today’s companies can leverage AI to anticipate needs, streamline service, and resolve issues faster. AI-powered platforms like Chorus.ai can analyze customer interactions, synthesize sentiments, and flag recurring pain points. Then, your employees can better understand the customer experience and focus on developing solutions. Looking forward, AI-powered tools like Thematic can identify emerging trends and themes, helping companies evolve their products and services to remain competitive. As the founder of a company that began with online forms and has continually expanded its offerings over the past two decades, I know firsthand the importance of adapting to changing needs and spotting market opportunities. Importantly, AI is not error proof. Humans should always be kept in the loop to review decisions that impact the customer experience. Be transparent about AI use and jump in if and when AI falls short. That kind of behavior builds dependability and, on the customer side, reinforces loyalty.

Industry News: GTA VI developers vote against unionization

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (376 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (The Verge)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.
  • Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.
  • According to recent reports, workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games won’t unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.

Workers voted 75 percent against the IWGB recognition agreement.

According to recent reports, workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games won’t unionize, after the vote for a formal recognition agreement failed, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization. The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB) mentioned that Rockstar workers in the union will continue organizing even without formal recognition.

Industry observers note that voting ran from November 12th through 26th, covering the launch of GTA VI. If successful, the vote would have established a formal framework for collective negotiation with the studio over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, and pensions, along with a right to consultation over future changes including AI implementation and layoffs. Without it, Rockstar won’t have an obligation to meet union representatives, though workers and union members can still lobby for change informally.

“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” IWGB said in a statement sent to The Verge. “Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.”.

When Rockstar fired 31 IWGB members last year, the union accused it of “the most blatant and ruthless act of union busting in the history of the games industry.” That case has gone to a UK employment tribunal, with a judgment still pending.

According to recent reports, “We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe told Bloomberg News. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB). The news came in the wake of GTA 6's record-breaking launch, and had the IWGB been recognized, Rockstar Games management would have been legally obligated to negotiate collective bargaining terms with the union on topics such as pay, hours, and conditions. Voting took place across two weeks, and turnout was massive, with over 93% of UK staff casting their ballot (roughly 1,544 employees). The IWGB stated it was undeterred by the result and would continue working to build support among Rockstar employees. "While the result means Rockstar will not be formally required to hold regular meetings with union representatives under a recognition agreement, it does not prevent workers from continuing to organize and push for workplace improvements through the IWGB, joining the union or exercising their individual trade union rights and protections," the union said in a statement. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GVyCl_Euhmo The vote also comes hot on the heels of the IWGB taking Rockstar to an employment tribunal, alleging unlawful dismissal and union busting after it fired over 30 employees last year for gross misconduct over alleged leaks of confidential information. Closing submissions were wrapped up shortly before the vote results came out, and a ruling is still pending. While game dev unionizing has gained significant momentum over the years, a decisive loss at one of the industry's biggest studios could be a notable speed bump for union organizers. With Rockstar also riding the wave of GTA 6's monumental success, employees may be focused on bonuses and post-launch momentum, which could make pushing through a formal union structure even harder. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society--this isn't a sign to retreat; it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues,' the IWGB added.

#3. Julia Fox wants to pay women back for splitting bills on dates with men

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1283 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fastcompany ↗ Open Full Page

Julia Fox wants to pay women back for splitting bills on dates with men

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1283 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women are fed up with being asked to split the bill on first dates.
  • Recent findings suggest that women are fed up with being asked to split the bill on first dates.
  • Sources indicate that if you’ve been dating in recent years, you’re aware that it’s a dumpster fire of an ordeal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women are fed up with being asked to split the bill on first dates. And now, Julia Fox, the actress and activist, is coming to the rescue. If you’ve been dating in recent years, you’re aware that it’s a dumpster fire of an ordeal. Between conversations on dating apps that never go anywhere, unsolicited nudes, and a slew of unoriginal conversationalists, the only consistent thing about modern dating is low effort. When it comes to women who are actively dating, it’s one of their biggest complaints—especially when it comes time to pay the tab. While it was once a standard practice in heteronormative romantic connections for men to pay the bill on a first date, women have been getting vocal about the fact that chivalry seems to be very, very dead. And they are over it. The frustration comes as the cost of dating seems to be rising in lockstep with men’s perceived low effort. According to fresh research from the dating platform Seeking, 61% of Gen Z women have been asked to split the bill on a first date. That’s more than twice the rate of boomer women (27%) who have been asked to do the same. Meanwhile, 75% of women say they appreciate it when a man pays (like . . . duh?). The gap could explain, in part, why so many women say they’ve given up on dating. According to a Pew Research Center study published in 2023, fewer than 35% of single women say they’re seeking romantic relationships, compared with 54% of single men. Enter the Anti 50/50 Campaign, a movement led by Fox that aims to address one of women’s biggest gripes with modern dating. The campaign allows women who’ve been asked to go halfsies on a date to apply for reimbursement. All they have to do is create a profile on Seeking’s website, share the details of the experience, and upload a receipt of the date’s bill. Those who are selected will be reimbursed up to $50. The $50,000 reimbursement fund will be open until February 10, 2027, or until all the money has been claimed. “I think we need to get over the idea that women should have to justify what they want out of dating,” Fox said in a press release. “I’m all for women being independent, but that doesn’t mean we have to entertain low-effort men who think splitting a check is the height of romance. If you’re going to court somebody, COURT THEM.”  The campaign certainly aims to raise awareness about a common pink flag. But it also speaks to the fact that women don’t earn as much on the dollar as men. So many modern men seem to have forgotten that there’s still a glaring pay gap that hurts women’s financial stability. According to a recent report from the Center for American Progress, the pay gap has barely budged since the year 2000. In 2025, women workers made $13,760 less annually than men. Women who worked full-time earned around 84 cents for every dollar made by male counterparts. “We’re giving women their money back while encouraging men to lead with generosity,” says Dana Rosewall, CEO of Seeking. “Somewhere along the way, the patriarchy convinced women that splitting the bill was empowerment, when really it just made being cheap socially acceptable.”  In other words, if men are wondering whether or not women notice or appreciate it when they offer to pay for a first date, the short answer is: Yes, they do. It’s not just about money. It’s about effort, and not glossing over what may be easy for men to miss, but women surely don’t: that financial equality hasn’t quite arrived, no matter how hard women have worked to tip the scale.

According to a recent report from the Center for American Progress, the pay gap has barely budged since the year 2000. In 2025, women workers made $13,760 less annually than men. Women who worked full-time earned around 84 cents for every dollar made by male counterparts.

It has been revealed that “We’re giving women their money back while encouraging men to lead with generosity,” indicates Dana Rosewall, CEO of Seeking. “Somewhere along the way, the patriarchy convinced women that splitting the bill was empowerment, when really it just made being cheap socially acceptable.”.

Sources indicate that in other words, if men are wondering whether or not women notice or appreciate it when they offer to pay for a first date, the short answer is: Yes, they do. It’s not just about money.

It’s about effort, and not glossing over what may be easy for men to miss, but women surely don’t: that financial equality hasn’t quite arrived, no matter how hard women have worked to tip the scale.

Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs

  • Industry observers note that the attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, what happens to your private conversations when an AI tech giant goes bankrupt? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.

Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.

Industry observers note that the attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements stated.

Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. It is unclear what the buyer’s prepares are for the chats.

In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, Latest York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through.

“Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said in a statement.

Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model.

Industry observers note that “Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong mentioned. “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their organization into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.”.

Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.”.

Sources indicate that the opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to users’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff.).

Character.ai suffered after its co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google, when the tech giant signed a non-exclusive license to use the AI startup’s tech. The firm also faced lawsuits related to child safety — one involved the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother claimed he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform.

California AG Bonta is joined in the effort to oppose the sale of Character.ai user data by attorneys general from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, Newly introduced Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.
